newsitem.title: JAPAN: Honda to post record profit on strong RV demand.
newsitem.headline: Honda to post record profit on strong RV demand.

text.p: Honda Motor Co Ltd, which has lately been shedding its image as a maker of sporty cars for that of a recreational vehicle (RV) company, will enjoy record profits due to a RV boom in Japan, analysts say.

The popularity of RVs, which now account for about half of Honda's car sales in Japan, has helped the company's vehicle sales for the April-September period shoot up by 23.1 percent from a year earlier.

"Honda's domestic sales of RVs, like the Step Wagon and CR-V, are higher than its initial target, and that should result in bigger cost cuts as it helps reduce the price of components," said Seiji Sugiura, an analyst of Nomura Research.
Honda will unveil its earnings for the April-September half-year on November 15.

Citing strong domestic sales, the company in August revised upwards its forecast for parent current profit for the half year to a record 60 billion yen ($526 million), up from a May forecast of 45 billion yen ($394 million) -- a huge jump from the 16.13 billion yen ($141 million) it posted a year earlier.

"Honda will post parent current profit of at least the estimated 60 billion yen ($526 million) in the half-year because of domestic sales and a weaker yen," Nobuaki Yanachi, senior analyst of Kankaku Research, said.
"I guess Honda's profit may exceed its projection but it could be this much (60 billion yen)," Nomura's Sugiura said.
Current profit is pretax profit and includes losses or gains on non-operational activities.

Meanwhile, the yen's recent weakness is also expected to have given Honda's profits a boost, since that made the company's foreign currency-denominated overseas revenue worth more in terms of yen. A decline of one yen ($0.08) against the dollar translates into six billion yen ($52.6 million) profit a year for the Honda group.
Honda had assumed an average rate of 105 yen ($0.92) to the dollar for this business year against 91 yen ($0.79) a year earlier. The dollar currently stands at around 114 yen ($1.00).

Honda's Odyssey minivan, which made its debut in October 1994 and triggered Japan's current boom in minivans, is still enjoying strong sales. All of the company's new RVs -- the CR-V light sport-utility vehicle, Orthia station wagon and Step Wagon eight-seat minivan -- are seeing good demand in Japan.

After its launch in May, sales of the Step Wagon rose to 15,481 units in October, surpassing Japan's biggest car maker Toyota Motor Corp's sales of 14,000 Corollas. The Step Wagon was the company's second best-selling model.

Honda also expects record profits for the full 1996/97 business year. In August, it raised its 1996/97 parent current forecast to 120 billion yen ($1.05 billion) from a May forecast of 90 billion yen ($789 million) and against a profit of 47.18 billion yen ($413 million) the year before.
Analysts are even more bullish than the company itself.

Nomura's Sugiura said Honda would exceed its own current profit forecast for 1996/97 by more than five billion yen ($43.8 million), while Nikko Research senior analyst Noriyuki Matsushima puts the total figure at 133 billion yen ($1.16 billion).
Kankaku's Yanachi, who forecasts Honda posting 140 billion yen ($1.22 billion) current profit this year, said profits would continue rising next year if the yen's weakness continues.

Matsushima, however, said the company's 1997/98 profits might not see such robust growth, adding: "Honda is now in a strong position but its profit may fall short next year, depending on the pace of erosion by rival makers' RVs into Honda's market share."
